title: The efficacious help is the delight that is greater: victorious delight
source_text: LXIII. Itaque illud efficax adjutorium divinae gratiae non in qualibet circa bonum delectatione ponit, sed in tali delectatione, quae in homine cui datur, omni delectatione opposita major sit, atque illam superet; & quam idcirco, cum Augustino, vocat Victricem delectationem. Si enim major sit carnis delectatio, nunquam illa quam spiritus infundit, a voluntate consensum impetrabit. Nam minor delectatio non potest majorem vincere: sed eam sequitur animus, quae magis eum afficiendo suavitate detinuerit. De gratia Christi salvat. lib. 4. cap. 6.
pass_a_gloss: LXIII. Therefore he places that efficacious help of divine grace not in any delight whatever about the good, but in such a delight, as in the man to whom it is given, is greater than every opposite delight, and overcomes it; and which therefore, with Augustine, he calls Victorious delight. For if the delight of the flesh be greater, never will that which the spirit infuses obtain consent from the will. For the lesser delight cannot conquer the greater: but the mind follows that which by affecting it more has held it with sweetness. On the grace of Christ the saviour book 4. chap. 6.
pass_b_english: Thesis LXIII. So he places that efficacious aid of divine grace not in just any delight in the good, but in a delight that, in the person to whom it is given, is greater than every opposing delight and overcomes it; and for this reason he calls it, with Augustine, 'victorious delight'.

If the delight of the flesh is greater, the delight that the spirit pours in will never win the will's consent. A lesser delight cannot overcome a greater; the mind follows whichever delight has held it more strongly by the sweetness with which it touches it. De gratia Christi Salvatoris, book 4, chapter 6.
